verdict.rationale: The evidence pack has no first-party documentation of Gmail masked or forwarding addresses that hide the user's real address. The only related material is community use of dot-variant and plus-address forms; these resolve to the real address and remain recognizable, so they do not stop sign-ups or strangers from learning it, and they count only as an adjacent user-side workaround. The masked-address feature mentioned in the pack belongs to a different provider, not Gmail.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can use aliases or masked addresses so sign-ups and strangers never learn my real address
